title: ForeSight-HF, a GPT-5 mini decision-support tool, scores two nursing-home heart-failure cases; patients managed independently
summary: Mount Sinai authors describe ForeSight-HF (GPT-5 mini on ProviderLoop) recommending diuresis for a warm/wet and de-escalation for a cold/dry nursing-home patient; both were managed independently.
account: Glajchen et al. (JACC: Case Reports, 3 June 2026) present ForeSight-HF, a clinical decision-support tool for heart-failure management in skilled nursing facilities. It uses OpenAI's GPT-5 mini, accessed late 2025, on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. It turns unstructured documentation into heart-failure likelihood scores, exacerbation risk scores and management recommendations. Physicians review them in weekly interdisciplinary meetings on the ProviderLoop platform. Two cases illustrate it: a congested, well-perfused patient for whom it recommended intensified diuresis, and a hypovolemic, hypoperfused patient for whom it recommended diuretic de-escalation. For each, the paper states that the patient remained at the facility for four months “managed independently of the AI system”. The disclosures state that platform infrastructure was provided by ProviderLoop and that Dr Bander is its founder and owner. Outcomes are not attributable to the system.
purpose: Generate heart-failure risk scores and management recommendations from nursing-facility documentation

deployer: Skilled nursing facilities served through the ProviderLoop platform (location not stated)
segment: Heart-failure patients in skilled nursing facilities

The only source is the vendor-affiliated case report; the senior author is the platform's founder and owner.
